issuer_id.description: Exact issuing actor. Its closed ActorId shape already contains the account or hosted-principal routing authority when one exists; no parallel principal-server sidecar is permitted.

items.description: Canonical action vocabulary. MUST be of the form ak.<segment>.<segment>... matching capabilities.md §5. Bare names without the ak. prefix are not permitted; consult capabilities.md before introducing new action names. Wildcards within a segment are not permitted in this schema; the resource selector controls scope, not action expansion.

constraints.description: Constraints applied to this grant. Re-grant control MUST be expressed via constraint_kind='authority_control' and max_authority_depth (see capabilities.md §10). A top-level 'delegable' field is forbidden and MUST be rejected as schema_violation. With no authority_control constraint the grant cannot be re-granted (equivalent to max_authority_depth=0).

issued_at.description: Grant issuance time — carries the 'creation time' semantics for a Capability Grant in place of the generic created_at (models/common-fields.md §3.2). Retention / audit / ordering queries MUST use issued_at / expires_at / revoked_at rather than falling back to created_at.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

updated_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp for the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

issuer_authority_refs.description: The authority this grant was issued under. Every grant has one: a root controller’s grant anchors on the authority-root cell, and any further grant anchors on the grants its issuer already holds. The typed ref is the only distinction within the unified grant shape. Authorization is recomputed from these refs on every decision, so revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants at read time without any cascading write.

oneOf.description: A grant the issuer holds. The issuer MUST be that grant's subject, and the ref MUST be active at evaluation time; its capability, resources and constraints all bound this child.

controller_epoch_at_issuance.description: The controller epoch under which this grant was issued. It proves the issuer controlled the root at issuance and nothing more: it is issuance audit, not a liveness version. Comparing it to the current epoch would make ak.realm.owner.transfer kill the whole authority tree.

authority_generation.description: The authority generation this grant is anchored to. Unlike the epoch this IS compared to the cell's current value: ak.realm.authority.reset advances it precisely so an entire authority tree stops resolving.

oneOf.description: The Realm authority-root cell. A rooted terminal: it never contributes an edge to the cycle check. realm_id is explicit rather than inherited from the envelope because ak.capability.derived can carry roots from another Realm.

authority_depth.description: Reducer-derived absolute distance from the authority root: a realm_root ref counts 0, so a root controller's grant is 1 and a member's re-grant is 2. Derived from the refs, never author-declared, so it cannot be misreported — which is what makes it safe to answer 'how far did this authority spread' with a single field instead of a recursive join. Taken at issuance and not recomputed on revocation; a later chain may be shorter than the recorded value, which is the conservative direction for a max_authority_depth decision.

authority_root_refs.description: Reducer-derived set of roots this grant ultimately descends from: the direct realm_root refs plus the union of every grant ref's own roots. Plural because multiple parents, and ak.capability.derived inheritance across a Realm link, can reach different roots or generations. Deduplicated on (realm_id, cell_ref, authority_generation) and sorted canonically by unsigned-byte order; controller_epoch_at_issuance is per-grant issuance audit and is deliberately not part of the identity key.

allOf.$comment: Lint condition (2) from capabilities.md §18.1: grants whose actions[] include moderator-role actions MUST carry a constraint with depends_on_moderation_state=true. Conditions (1) and (3) (subject condition selector referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue/cell) are reducer-side lint and not enforced here.
